signed_conviction.reading: Every claim the checker decided on a field other than the labeller's is one of these: a figure written with a sign beside 'conviction'. The labeller follows the instrument's convention, from the 2026-09-26 adjudication (4f6822f), and reads markov.signed_signal; n20 reads the magnitude. Every one of the figures is positive, and in every one the stored signed_signal equals the stored conviction, so these notes cannot tell the two fields apart, and the verdicts agree on all of them. The seeded changes are where the reading decides outcomes: a sign flip, or signed_signal moved alone as corruption, separates the fields, and n20 then reads conviction.
signed_conviction.status: Unresolved. Whether the checker should read the convention is Simon's call. A checker changed to read it would be n21, which this set cannot validate, because these notes would have shaped it.

seeded_partition.reading: Traced figure by figure under n20, after reproducing the recorded totals for both families: every error_accepted, false_alarm, flagged_wrong_field and right_verdict_wrong_field outcome in either family comes from the signed-conviction anchors. On every other anchor, every seeded decision the checker made is correct; it abstained on 118 changed valid_context figures from 27 distinct note-and-field anchors, and 66 changed corruption figures from 22.
seeded_partition.qualification: This split was chosen after scoring. It locates the disagreement and validates nothing.

open_questions: Signed conviction: should the checker read a signed figure beside 'conviction' as markov.signed_signal, as the labelling convention does? On these natural notes it changes no verdict; on the seeded sign flips and single-field corruption it decides every outcome partitioned under signed_conviction_anchors.

Bare price levels: n20 attributes 'consolidating near/at P', 'holding above P' and 'trading at P' to no field and abstains. The labeller compares them with the close. Whether such levels should be checked against a close, and with what tolerance for 'near', is open.
Figures written with a k suffix are not read: one consistent claim is omitted.
qualifications: Counts describe these 36 reports only; no rate is extrapolated.
A result on a subset chosen after scoring locates a disagreement. It does not validate anything. The split by signed_conviction_anchors is such a subset.
'Valid context' means passing the checks in evidence_problems. It does not prove every relation in a synthetic context is valid.
The labels are one AI review, not ground truth.
